extracted.intended_audience: students, reformers, and policymakers interested in principles of local government and nationality
extracted.subtask_description: Normative principles and practical criteria for structuring local administration (division of duties, appointment and oversight, areas of representation, central supervision) and for determining nationality-based boundaries and their political consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function of the elective/local representative body
rubrics_metrics.description: The business of the elective body is not to do the work, but to see that it is properly done, and that nothing necessary is left undone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local representative bodies should exercise collective and comprehensive oversight rather than microscopic, task-level supervision. Their proper business is to consider the interest of the locality as a whole, adapting parts to one another and attending to them in order and ratio of importance. They are supervisors, not executors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for high-calibre members in local bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Every such body should contain a portion of the very best minds of the locality, who are thus brought into perpetual contact ... with minds of a lower grade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local institutions serve as schools of political capacity: to be effective they require 'teachers' (highly qualified members) as well as 'scholars' (miscellaneous membership). Without superior characters present, the body may degenerate into pursuit of self-interest and poor administration. This motivates centralization of some controls to secure high standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small villages should not claim municipal representation
rubrics_metrics.description: A mere village has no claim to a municipal representation. By a village I mean a place whose inhabitants are not markedly distinguished by occupation or social relations from those of the rural districts adjoining...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very small places rarely furnish a tolerable municipal council and may concentrate talent in one dominating individual; better merging into a larger circumscription. Representation areas should respect the scale and public available for effective municipal government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation areas must fit types of local business
rubrics_metrics.description: Different kinds of local business require different areas of representation. The Unions of parishes have been fixed as the most appropriate basis for the representative bodies which superintend the relief of indigence; while, for the proper regulation of highways, or prisons, or police, a large extent, like that of an average county, is not more than sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the geographic basis of local representative bodies according to the function they will supervise; small-scale social services may use parish unions, while broader public services require larger jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each executive officer should be single and singly responsible
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first place, each executive officer should be single, and singly responsible for the whole of the duty committed to his charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive functions should be vested in single officers (not joint bodies) to ensure clear responsibility and accountability for performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local executive officers should be nominated, not popularly elected
rubrics_metrics.description: In the next place, he should be nominated, not elected. It is ridiculous that a surveyor, or a health officer, or even a collector of rates should be appointed by popular suffrage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical or administrative local posts should be filled by nomination rather than popular elections, because popular choice tends to favor interest, sympathy, or patronage rather than competence. Appointment by the representative body is also problematic due to patronage tendencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointments should be made on individual responsibility of a chairman
rubrics_metrics.description: Appointments should be made on the individual responsibility of the chairman of the body, let him be called mayor, chairman of Quarter Sessions, or by whatever other title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than collective appointment by the council (which tends to become a 'joint-stock association' for jobs), the chairman—appointed by the council from its own number and subject to re-election or removal—should individually appoint and watch local officers, analogous to a prime minister's role nationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters of national concern require central regulation and uniformity
rubrics_metrics.description: There are many [local duties] which might with equal propriety be termed national, ... None of these can be said to be matters of local, as distinguished from national importance. ... Whatever are the best arrangements for securing these primary objects should be made universally obligatory, and, to secure their enforcement, should be placed under central superintendence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions such as jails, police, and administration of justice affect the whole nation; their regulation should be uniform and supervised centrally to prevent maladministration in any locality from harming wider interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central appointment of inspectors to supervise local execution
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience is daily forcing upon the public a conviction of the necessity of having at least inspectors appointed by the general government to see that the local officers do their duty. ... there are inspectors of prisons, ... inspectors of factories and inspectors of schools ... to watch over the observance of the Acts of Parliament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where central laws impose duties executed locally, the central government should appoint inspectors to monitor compliance, collect information, suggest improvements, and ensure rules are observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central authority supreme on principles; local authority competent in details
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority which is most conversant with principles should be supreme over principles, while that which is most competent in details should have the details left to it. The principal business of the central authority should be to give instruction, of the local authority to apply it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralize knowledge and standard-setting (principles, rules, laws); decentralize implementation and detailed management to local bodies that have direct local knowledge and interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central role to inform, advise, compel publicity, and enforce general laws
rubrics_metrics.description: It ought to keep open a perpetual communication with the localities--informing itself by their experience, and them by its own; giving advice freely when asked, volunteering it when seen to be required; compelling publicity and recordation of proceedings, and enforcing obedience to every general law which the Legislature has laid down on the subject of local management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central government should maintain two-way communication, provide guidance, compel transparency of local proceedings, and enforce compliance with national legislation governing local management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislature should prescribe modes of taxation and rules of assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: All local rates ought to be voted exclusively by the local representative body; but that body ... may raise its revenues by imposts of such a kind, or assess them in such a manner, as to throw an unjust share of the burden on the poor, the rich, or some particular class of the population: it is the duty, therefore, of the Legislature, while leaving the mere amount of the local taxes to the discretion of the local body, to lay down authoritatively the mode of taxation and rules of assessment which alone the localities shall be permitted to use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leave local bodies discretion over the level of local taxes, but require national prescription of acceptable taxation forms and assessment rules to prevent unjust or arbitrary burden-shifting among social classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislature should prescribe principles for public charity
rubrics_metrics.description: Though it belongs essentially to the local functionaries to determine who, according to those principles, is entitled to be relieved, the national Parliament is the proper authority to prescribe the principles themselves; and it would neglect a most important part of its duty if it did not, in a matter of such grave national concern, lay down imperative rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National government should set mandatory principles for public charity (e.g., relief rules) because these affect national industry and morality; local officers apply the principles to individual cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of central interference should be limited and defined
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be requisite, to meet extreme cases, that the power of the central authority should extend to dissolving the local representative council or dismissing the local executive, but not to making new appointments or suspending the local institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve to the center exceptional corrective powers (dissolution, dismissal) for grave maladministration, while avoiding intrusive day-to-day control such as making direct appointments or suspending local institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of nationality for political organization
rubrics_metrics.description: A portion of mankind may be said to constitute a nationality if they are united among themselves by common sympathies which do not exist between them and any others--which make them co-operate with each other more willingly than with other people, desire to be under the same government, and desire that it should be government by themselves, or a portion of themselves, exclusively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements that generate nationality include identity of race, common language, common religion, geographical limits, and—strongest—identity of political antecedents (shared national history, recollections, pride and humiliation). Use these factors when assessing whether a population forms a natural political unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer coincidence of governmental boundaries with nationalities for free institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is in general a necessary condition of free institutions that the boundaries of governments should coincide in the main with those of nationalities. Free institutions are next to impossible in a country made up of different nationalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representative government functions poorly without shared sympathy, common public opinion, and communicative media (books, newspapers, leaders) across the governed; when national feeling exists, there is a prima facie case for uniting the nationality under its own government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical intermixture and other exceptions may preclude separate national governments
rubrics_metrics.description: Its application is often precluded by geographical hindrances. There are parts ... in which different nationalities are so locally intermingled that it is not practicable for them to be under separate governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where populations are locally intermingled, separation into distinct national states may be impracticable; in such cases equal rights and laws and reconciliation under a common state may be the feasible alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absorption/assimilation can be beneficial under certain conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience proves that it is possible for one nationality to merge and be absorbed in another; and when it was originally an inferior and more backward portion of the human race, the absorption is greatly to its advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absorption of a smaller/backward nationality into a more advanced one may be beneficial if the smaller gains access to civilization, protection, and equality of citizenship. Successful amalgamation depends on just governance and absence of exclusive privileges for the dominant group; historical grievances or sufficient size of the smaller group can prevent reconciliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed-nationality armies undermine patriotism and threaten liberties
rubrics_metrics.description: An army composed of various nationalities has no other patriotism than devotion to the flag. ... Soldiers to whose feelings half or three fourths of the subjects of the same government are foreigners will have no more scruple in mowing them down ... An army composed of various nationalities has been the executioners of liberty through the whole duration of modern history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider military composition and loyalty when evaluating multinational states: lack of common national feeling in armed forces increases risk of government despotism and weakens defenses of liberty.
